content.intro: This lesson covers building bigger fastapi applications within structuring and configuring applications. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use building bigger fastapi applications to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Building Bigger FastAPI Applications matters because it is part of structuring and configuring applications. In practice, focus on predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Why a single-file application becomes difficult to maintain

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Building Bigger FastAPI Applications
content_blocks.code:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.ready = True
    yield
    app.state.ready = False

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
content_blocks.expected_output: The lifespan setup runs before requests are served and cleanup runs at shutdown.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
